title: Calcium imaging with GCaMP
objective: Explain how GCaMP reports neural activity and why calcium is a proxy.

steps.title: Calcium as a stand-in for firing
steps.body: When a neuron fires, voltage-gated channels let **Ca²⁺** rush in. **[[GCaMP]]** is a protein that glows brighter when it binds calcium. So a rise in GCaMP fluorescence (**[[ΔF/F|ΔF/F]]**) reports that the neuron was active — an indirect but powerful readout.

steps.prompt: What does a rise in GCaMP fluorescence indicate?
options: Intracellular calcium rose, which usually reflects activity
The neuron simply took up more of the dye than before
The cell made more GCaMP protein during the recording
Calcium was pumped out of the cell, lighting the sensor
steps.explanation: GCaMP brightens when calcium binds; calcium entry follows firing, so brightness tracks activity.

options: It became active, so calcium rose inside it
It pumped calcium out, which lights the sensor
It made a sudden burst of new GCaMP protein
variants.reveal: A fluorescence rise reflects calcium influx from activity.

steps.setup: You apply capsaicin to GCaMP+ cultured DRG neurons.
steps.reveal: Capsaicin opens **[[TRPV1]]**, so only TRPV1-expressing neurons take up calcium and brighten — calcium imaging reads out which subtypes respond.

variants.prompt: Capsaicin on GCaMP+ DRG culture brightens…
variants.explanation: Only TRPV1+ cells respond to capsaicin with calcium influx.

steps.title: Calcium is slow
steps.body: Calcium rises and falls more slowly than a spike, so GCaMP shows *that* and roughly *how much* a neuron fired, not the exact spike times. For millisecond timing you still need electrical recording.

flag.note: GCaMP variants differ in speed/sensitivity; it reports calcium, an indirect proxy for spiking.

sources.note: GCaMP6 genetically encoded calcium indicators for imaging activity.
